messages.author: eafa26121223327e
messages.subject: Missing detection covariates
parts:
I'm running N-mixture models in unmarked on about 7 years of count data.  The count data varies between having 2 visits (counts) and 3 visits.  I understand that it is possible to run and compare (via AIC) these models in unmarked despite the discrepancy in visit numbers.  However, I am trying to model detection covariates that accompany these visits - specifically the time of the survey. Unmarked recognizes the lack of a time #3 on the sites with only 2 visits as missing data.  Has anyone else run into this problem, and if so, have they found a way to deal with this issue without either a) not modeling that covariate or b) modeling the 2 visit and 3 visit counts separately?

Thanks

messages.author: b655697c64cc729d
messages.subject: Re: Missing detection covariates
parts:
Hi Kaylan- Does it make any difference in the estimates if you insert different values as those NA covariate values? I would assume it doesn't. If you are missing covariates where you have response variable data, you can use the mean covariate value as long you are not missing a lot of covariate data. 
Myles

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Missing detection covariates
parts:
hi Kaylan,
 If I understand what you're saying then I would say all of your AIC values for any model should be directly comparable to one another. i.e., if the data set is exactly the same for each model, with the same pattern of missing values, then everything should be ok.   One thing to be careful of is comparing AIC across different models when some of the covariate values are missing. In that case, AIC will not be comparable because unmarked will remove records which are associated with missing covariate values.
regards
andy

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Missing detection covariates
parts:
hi Kaylan,
 you can compare all models with or without covariates by AIC. The only problem would be if your count data were non-missing but the covariate was missing.  In that case if you fit a model without the covariate the AIC will be  based on all of the data. But if you fit a model with the covariate then it will be based on the data minus the values having missing covariates. 
You don't have this problem b/c the data are missing whenever your covariate values are missing.

regards
andy
